newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dasa still hopes for Fokker rescue.
newsitem.headline: Dasa still hopes for Fokker rescue.

text.p: Court-appointed administrators are to wind up bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV after Shorts, part of Canada's Bombardier group, said it would no longer supply aeroplane parts, Dutch ANP news agency said on Thursday.

Meanwhile, in Bonn, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, which holds an indirect stake in Fokker N.V., said it hoped that the Dutch planemaker could still be saved but it was prepared for Fokker to be wound up.

Court-appointed Dutch administrators rated the chances of Fokker's survival as "minimal" after Bombardier unit Shorts pulled out of delivering wings for Fokker aircraft, leading rescue talks with Korea's Samsung Aerospace to fail.
The administrators said there was very little chance of an alternative rescue plan going ahead with another supplier of wings.
"The chances that the Fokker (aircraft) programme could survive on the basis of such a plan are minimal," they said in a statement.
"It goes without saying that Fokker...will continue to make aircraft already ordered by KLM Cityhopper, Vietnam Airlines and Ethiopian Airlines," they said.
The administrators said that under an agreement with Fokker suppliers, they had been able to keep open supply lines from firms such as Shorts until October 31.
Although talks with Samsung had initially made good progress they had run into delays in late October, administrators said.

"As a result, the crucial date of October 31 passed without orders being placed with suppliers and without a memorandum of understanding on a "new" Fokker between Samsung, the (Dutch) state, Stork and administrators."
In July, industrial services group Stork NV bought Fokker's profitable aircraft maintenance activities.
